output.reasoning: The posting fails three of the labeling criteria. (1) Role type: 'Applied AI Architect' is a customer-facing pre-sales role. The work is being a trusted technical advisor to enterprises, partnering with account executives, delivering technical content to executives, and travelling to customer sites. It is not hands-on building, training, and deploying ML/NLP systems, so it does not match her target roles (ML Engineer, AI Engineer, Applied NLP Engineer, Research Engineer). (2) Level: the qualifications explicitly ask for '10+ years of experience in technical customer-facing roles such as Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, or Technical Account Manager'. That is far beyond the 3+ year cutoff for a new grad finishing an MS at Boston University in 2026-12 with one ML Engineer co-op. (3) Location: the role is in Bangalore, India, serving India and APAC customers. It is not US-based and is not designated Remote, and her willingness to relocate covers only the US. Skills: the qualifications name few specific technologies ('Comfortable with Python' plus general LLM frameworks and cloud architecture), so the skills test is not decisive. Python does overlap with her shipped skills, and her RAG and eval experience is loosely related to helping customers build evaluation frameworks. Sponsorship: the posting says 'We do sponsor visas!', so sponsorship is not disqualifying. However, the role type, the explicit 10+ year requirement, and the non-US location each independently make this NOT_RELEVANT.
